title: A shared cost split over the targets of an allocation rule (PRD-001 FR-DIM-03, ALLOC-PRORATA)
description: One case both implementations must reproduce. The amount (any sign, at most the currency's minor units) is split over the targets by weights, and what the key cannot place is a last part of its own, unallocated, that stays on the source account. ALLOC-PRORATA: each part gets the whole minor units of its exact share, then the units left go one each to the largest fractional remainders, a tie to the earlier part, the unallocated part last of all; the parts and the unallocated part add to the amount. The key turns the targets into weights: weights are whole numbers (a headcount; unplaced is the people with no department), percent are percentages above nothing with at most two decimals adding to at most 100 (the unallocated weight is what they leave of 100), quantity are usage quantities of zero or more with at most six decimals (unplaced is the usage the file could not place).

unplaced.description: The unallocated weight in the key's own unit; for percent it is what the percentages leave, so it is not given.
